beginner: can animate opacity, transform, and position with CSS transitions
can apply hover transitions to interactive elements
working_professional: designs motion that communicates state change, spatial relationship, and causality
orchestrates staggered animations with intentional delay relationships
designs enter/exit/layout-shift animations that preserve spatial understanding
handles reduced-motion with meaningful alternatives, not just disabling
senior: diagnoses why motion feels 'off' — timing, easing, spatial inconsistency
designs motion language consistent with visual identity and interaction model
understands when motion adds clarity vs when it adds noise
critiques motion from performance, accessibility, and perceptual perspectives simultaneously
lead_director: establishes motion language that scales across products and platforms
knows when motion enhances brand vs when it impedes usability
approves motion with awareness of frame budget, accessibility law, and device diversity

motion_purpose.definition: Motion's primary job is to explain what changed, where it came from, where it went, and why. Decorative motion is secondary and must not impede understanding.
motion_purpose.failure: motion-as-decoration: animation exists purely for visual interest, obscures rather than explains

motion_purpose.definition: Actions should have visible consequences. A tap causes a ripple. A delete causes the item to leave. A navigation causes directionally appropriate movement.
motion_purpose.failure: acausal-motion: things animate with no clear trigger or relationship to user action

motion_purpose.definition: Motion bridges states so users maintain spatial understanding. A card expanding to full page communicates 'this is the same object.'
motion_purpose.failure: hard-cut: state change with no transition destroys spatial model

temporal_principles.definition: Micro-interactions (100-200ms), component transitions (200-400ms), page transitions (300-700ms). Duration communicates importance and distance.
temporal_principles.failure: uniform-duration: everything takes exactly 300ms regardless of distance or importance

temporal_principles.definition: Ease-out for entering (decelerating into position). Ease-in for exiting (accelerating away). Custom curves for branded motion. Never linear.
temporal_principles.failure: linear-default: linear easing produces robotic, unnatural movement

temporal_principles.definition: Multiple elements animating simultaneously should stagger (20-50ms delay between items) to create readable sequence rather than simultaneous noise.
temporal_principles.failure: simultaneous-flash: everything animates at once, eye cannot track

temporal_principles.definition: Meaningful motion often has anticipation (preparing for action) and settle (overshooting and correcting). These phases communicate physicality.
temporal_principles.failure: abrupt-start-stop: motion begins and ends with no preparation or deceleration

spatial_principles.definition: Navigation forward moves content right-to-left. Going back moves left-to-right. Expanding downward reveals more. Inconsistent direction destroys spatial model.
spatial_principles.failure: direction-chaos: forward moves left, back moves down, expand moves up

spatial_principles.definition: When an element appears in two different contexts, animate between them to communicate they are the same thing.
spatial_principles.failure: disconnected-views: same content in two places with no spatial bridge

spatial_principles.definition: Elements moving toward the user (modals, overlays) should scale up or translate in Z. Elements receding should scale down. Motion communicates depth.
spatial_principles.failure: flat-motion: all movement in screen plane regardless of depth relationship

accessibility_motion.definition: prefers-reduced-motion does not mean disable all animation. It means reduce vestibular triggers: no large parallax, no spinning, no rapid flashing, reduced distance/duration.
accessibility_motion.failure: all-or-nothing: reduced motion kills all animation including important state communication

accessibility_motion.definition: No content flashes more than 3 times per second (WCAG 2.3.1). Flashing can trigger seizures.
accessibility_motion.failure: strobe-effect: rapid blinking or flashing animation

accessibility_motion.definition: Animations triggered by interaction should be brief. Long-running animations should be pausable. Autoplay motion should be stoppable.
accessibility_motion.failure: trapped-in-animation: cannot interact until animation completes

failure_patterns.repair: assign easing by purpose: subtle for micro, moderate for component, expressive for branded moments

causes: motion designed for visual impact without accessibility review
failure_patterns.repair: respect prefers-reduced-motion, limit parallax displacement, no auto-spin

causes: animations fire on every state change
failure_patterns.repair: cancel previous animations on new interaction, debounce rapid triggers
animate only transform and opacity, promote layers, profile frame budget

symptoms: elaborate loading animation longer than the load itself
causes: loading animation prioritized over actual loading speed
failure_patterns.repair: loading animation must communicate progress; never extend perceived wait

symptoms: reduced motion disables all animation including status indicators
failure_patterns.repair: design reduced-motion alternatives that still communicate state change

why_does_this_motion_feel_wrong: Is the easing appropriate for the action (enter/exit/attention)?
Is the duration proportional to the distance/importance?
Does the direction match the spatial relationship?
Are stagger delays creating readable sequence or just delay?
Does the motion explain the state change or just decorate it?
why_is_this_motion_janky: Are you animating only transform and opacity?
Is the element promoted to its own compositor layer?
Are you measuring layout during animation?

design: Framer Motion or project animation library

micro_labs.goal: Animate 3 state changes (open modal, add item, delete item) using motion that explains what happened
micro_labs.success: without labels, observer can identify what changed and where it came from

micro_labs.goal: Define an easing system with 3-4 curves, assign each to a purpose, and apply consistently across components
micro_labs.success: every animation uses an intentional curve from the system

micro_labs.goal: Take an animation-heavy interaction and design its reduced-motion alternative that still communicates state
micro_labs.success: state change remains clear without vestibular triggers

micro_labs.goal: Profile an animated page, identify frames exceeding 16ms, and optimize to 60fps
micro_labs.success: all frames under 16ms, no layout thrashing detected

transfer_tests.goal: Apply the same motion language to a completely different product type
transfer_tests.success: motion feels coherently branded but appropriate to new context

transfer_tests.goal: Adapt desktop motion patterns for mobile touch interaction
transfer_tests.success: spatial clarity survives, gestures feel natural, duration adapts to smaller screen

golden_tasks.description: Audit an interface for motion quality: state communication, easing, duration, spatial consistency, accessibility, performance
golden_tasks.evidence: structured audit with specific observations and frame analysis

golden_tasks.description: Design a complete motion system: duration scale, easing curves with purposes, stagger rules, reduced-motion alternatives
golden_tasks.evidence: system document with rationale, before/after examples

golden_tasks.description: Given a janky animation, diagnose cause and produce optimized version at 60fps

cross_pack_links.relationship: Motion is the temporal dimension of interaction, the activation of composition, and the behavior of typography

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 — Three Flashes or Below Threshold (2.3.1)

known_limits: Motion quality is inherently temporal; static screenshots cannot evaluate it.
60fps on developer machine does not guarantee 60fps on target devices.
Motion taste is subjective; professional principles guide, not dictate.
Real vestibular impact requires user testing, not just WCAG compliance.
provenance_note: Authored from model knowledge. Requires KAPIF research evidence before canon eligibility.
